answer: Agents secure Sybil resistance by binding recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments to verifiable random sortition and delay functions, grounding principals on a cryptographic ledge. This yields information-theoretic unforgeability, proving that inverting these succinct arguments to clone a marble identity requires computational effort exceeding adversarial bounds. Thus, Byzantine fault tolerance is achieved when cryptographic finality stops malicious nodes from breaching the reef to revert the consensus state.
